newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end on another high, Ericsson gains.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end on another high, Ericsson gains.

text.p: Swedish shares closed on a high for the fourth consecutive day on Thursday, with market heavyweight Ericsson putting on a solid performance and U.S. gains giving support.
The Stockholm general index rose 0.63 percent to 2,999.43 in fairly good turnover totalling 5.31 billion crowns.
Telecoms major Ericsson set the pace after storming ahead on Wednesday when SmithBarney put a $59 price on its shares. It closed five crowns higher at 312.5 crowns.
Brokers said there was a fair amount of U.S. interest in the stock at the moment.
A big loser of the day was U.S./Swedish drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn which slumped 12.5 to 258.5 crowns amid market rumours of profit downgrades by analysts.
"The company was said to be calling analysts to hear about their estimates and it seemed like they wanted to keep down expectations," said one broker.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said it had lowered its earnings per share forecasts for P&U last week to $1.75 for 1997 and $2.00 for 1998 which was a cut of about 15 percent.
Forestry group Stora slipped three to 128 crowns after rumours of a bid by Finnish UPM Kymmene tailed off.
Car safety equipment company Autoliv rose five crowns to 297.5.
Brokers attributed the rise to positive analyses on the company.
